Owner's-Earnings DCF Ranking — 2026-10-14

Sweep progress: 111 analyzed of 2617 companies under $40B + pilot exceptions. Ranked by probability-weighted implied IRR at current price. Tap a company name for its detail page.
How to read this

Each company gets a five-scenario owner's-earnings DCF (super bear / bear / base / bull / super bull, each with an assigned likelihood); growth fades over a moat-driven competitive advantage period. Wtd IRR = probability-weighted expected annual return at the current price. IV = probability-weighted intrinsic value per share at a 15% discount rate; Upside = IV vs price. Tiers: S ≥25% · A 20-25% · B 15-20% (clears the 15% hurdle) · C 10-15% · D <10% · F no positive owner's earnings. Screening-grade standardized DCF — read the company folder's analysis.md before acting.

Filing gaps filled by a main-agent judgment override — an override never replaces a filed value.

FieldValueKindSourcePeriods filled
capex$143MfilingForm 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025, Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows, investing activities line 'Capital expenditures, net': $143M for FY2025, with $216M for FY2024 in the same statement (corroborated by the filer's 10-Q cash-flow statements: $87M for the nine months ended Sep 30, 2025 and $131M for the nine months ended Sep 30, 2024, with Q4 adding the remainder in each year)2024-12-31, 2025-12-31

Measured impact on the 3-year median base actually used (no override → with override): base OE/share $20.88 → $20.03 (-4.09%) · weighted IRR 12.7% → 11.8% (-0.88pp)

This override is the only reason this company has a tier. Without it, the filing gap blocks scoring entirely — the judgment call is the whole verdict.

capex: DATA_GAP:capex — capex missing for FY2024 and FY2025 of the last 3 in EDGAR companyfacts under every candidate tag the engine reads (the filed values through FY2023 came via PaymentsToAcquireProductiveAssets, $256M in FY2023). The engine applies this single FY2025 filing value to both missing periods; for FY2024 it understates true capex by $73M (~2% of that year's conservative OE, raising that year's OE — noted, not hidden), and capex at this level is immaterial to the verdict either way: FY2025 capex is ~4.8% of OCF and ~5% of conservative OE. ttm.py could not use the override to build a TTM base (it exits on a missing post-FY SBC YTD fact), so the override's effect is on the FY median base only.

Moat

9/10 Competitive advantage period 13.7 yrs
Strengths
  • +Exclusive .com/.net registry operator under ICANN agreements with presumptive renewal — no competitor can legally take the registry without a contract change
  • +.com is the default commercial TLD: brand identity, email, and links are embedded in 179.1M registrations — switching costs are borne by registrants, not Verisign, and renewal rates run ~76% despite repeated price hikes
  • +Proven contractual pricing power: wholesale .com price taken from $7.85 to $10.26 since 2021, next +7% to $10.97 effective Nov 1, 2026, with up to three more 7% steps to 2030; .net allows up to 10%/yr
  • +Structural cost advantage: ~68% operating margins, capex of only $22.8M on $1,656.6M FY2025 revenue — registry scale economics no entrant can replicate
  • +29 years of 100% .com/.net DNS availability — operational record is itself a barrier to any re-bid argument
Pressures
  • −Moat is granted by ICANN/NTIA contracts, not owned — .com agreement runs to Nov 2030 and pricing terms are a political/antitrust target (NTIA publicly wanted lower .com prices at the 2024 renewal; antitrust suit filed over .com pricing)
  • −Mature .com base — long-run volume growth depends on new-business formation; alternative TLDs (.ai, ccTLDs), brand TLDs from ICANN's 2026 round, and platform/social presence substitute at the margin
  • −Wholesale price hikes are capped (7% in only 4 of each 6 years for .com) and each hike risks registrar/registrant pushback and volume elasticity
  • −Single-product concentration — essentially all economics are .com/.net registry fees; a DNS security/availability failure would be existential for the contract

shares: DATA_GAP:shares — diluted shares missing for FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025 in EDGAR companyfacts (the filer tags recent share counts with Class A/Class B dimensions that the aggregated facts drop, so the engine filed no share value for any period in its 2016-2025 history). The filer's own FY2025 diluted weighted-average count fills the gap; the engine applies this single value to every missing period, so the 3-yr median base is the FY2024 OE total divided by this count — within ~2% of the FY2024 figure on its own filed count (2,798M) — and the direction is conservative (a shrinking count applied to earlier years understates their OE/share).

  • +Fortress liquidity: cash and investments of RMB283.1 billion at June 30, 2026 (Q2 2026 results), funding AI capex, a $5B buyback through 2028 and a first dividend policy without balance-sheet stress

  • −Legacy search advertising is in structural decline: online marketing services revenue -19% YoY in Q2 2026 (-22% in Q1 2026), as budgets shift to Douyin/short video, Xiaohongshu and super-apps

  • −Cloud and models are contested, not owned: Alibaba, Tencent, Huawei and ByteDance compete on price and distribution; ERNIE's model lead must be re-earned each generation
  • −China/VIE/regulatory overhang: VIE structure, PRC data and platform regulation, US ADS delisting tail risk, and a 2026 US securities class action over AI-revenue disclosures
  • −Controlled, cash-hungry subsidiaries and investments: iQIYI revenue -5% YoY in Q2 2026 with a working-capital deficit disclosed in the 20-F; FY2025 group operating cash flow turned negative

sbc: EDGAR companyfacts carries no SBC figure for Fortis under any candidate tag (ShareBasedCompensation, AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense, ifrs AdjustmentsForSharebasedPayments) for any filed year — sbc_tag is blank for 2016-2025 — so the v5 data gate gaps SBC for FY2023-2025. Moat

5/10 Competitive advantage period None yrs
Strengths
  • +Regulated franchise monopolies — exclusive electric/gas service territories across five Canadian provinces, ten U.S. states and the Caribbean
  • +Visible rate-base growth: $28.8B 2026-2030 capital plan driving ~7% midyear rate-base CAGR ($42.4B 2025 to $57.9B 2030 guided)
  • +Diversification across 10 utilities and multiple regulators — no single rate case decides the company
  • +52 consecutive years of common dividend increases; 4-6% annual dividend growth guided through 2030
  • +Essential-service demand with low cyclicality; earnings grew through rate-base additions in 2025 and H1 2026
Pressures
  • −Returns are capped at regulator-allowed ROEs — no pricing power; FERC's Oct 2024 MISO base ROE decision cut ITC earnings retroactively ($20M hit to 2024)
  • −Regulatory lag: costs of rate-base growth not yet in customer rates already pressure UNS Energy earnings
  • −Heavy leverage (net debt $24.47B per dcf_numbers.json) and rate-sensitive funding costs
  • −Perpetual equity issuance via the dividend reinvestment plan dilutes share count (~+1.7%/yr share CAGR in the engine blend)
  • −Political/regulatory exposure across many jurisdictions plus CAD/USD translation exposure

capex: DATA_GAP:capex — capex missing for FY2023, FY2024, FY2025 (and every other year) in EDGAR companyfacts under every candidate tag the engine reads, because the filer reports capex only under its own extension tag (same dead end as TKO in the system README). sbc: DATA_GAP:sbc — SBC missing for FY2023, FY2024, FY2025 in EDGAR companyfacts under both tags the engine reads (the allocated tag's facts stop in 2014). The filing's own Note 21 table reports stock-based compensation expense for all three years ($48M / $54M / $60M). The engine applies this single FY2025 value ($60M) to every missing period, overstating FY2023 SBC by $12M and FY2024 by $6M — immaterial against OCF of $3.2-3.6B and in the conservative direction.

Moat

6/10 Competitive advantage period None yrs
Strengths
  • +Franchised regulated electric and gas monopolies in Michigan — DTE Electric serves ~2.3M customers in southeastern Michigan; captive, essential-service demand
  • +Rate-base model: the $36.5B 2026-2030 capital plan enters rate base and earns an authorized return; management guides 6-8% operating EPS growth through 2030
  • +Large-load growth: 1.4 GW Oracle data-center project approved and under construction, plus an executed 1.0 GW Google agreement (pending MPSC approval)
  • +Recovery mechanisms (including the Infrastructure Recovery Mechanism for distribution spend) shorten the lag between capex and rate recovery
Pressures
  • −Regulator caps economics: the MPSC sets allowed ROE and recovery, and the FY2025 10-K records disallowances of previously recorded capex written off in 2023 and 2024 — no pricing power beyond rate cases
  • −Affordability politics: data-center and clean-energy transition costs recovered from existing customers invite rate-case pushback
  • −Balance sheet and dilution: net debt $25,098M, and planned $500-600M/yr of equity issuance through 2028 on top of a +1.84%/yr share-count CAGR
  • −Coal retirement (all coal by 2032 per the 2026 IRP, search results) and clean-energy mandates force transition capex whose full recovery is not guaranteed
